judgment.rationale: Both Visual Studio generations fail on the same laptop while other apps work, so compare app eligibility and elevation rather than assuming a Visual Studio 2026 regression.
evidence: The report names PowerToys 0.102.3101 and Visual Studio 2026 18.11.4 on Windows 11.
A follow-up reports the same behavior in Visual Studio 2022 17.14.45 on the same installation.
The reporter runs PowerToys elevated and tried removing exclusions; the attached settings enable Shift-drag and snap-hotkey override.
judgment.recommended_action: Compare both IDE versions and a normal app on one test profile with controlled privilege levels.

issue_context.summary: FancyZones cannot place either reported Visual Studio version, though other apps still snap on the affected laptop.
known_information: The reporter tried drag and hotkeys and saw native Windows Snap instead. Clearing the exclusions list did not help.
PowerToys runs elevated; the attached settings enable Shift-drag and snap-hotkey override.
inferences: Different window eligibility or process elevation could explain the app-specific failure. Neither has been established.
issue_context.analysis: Keep the layout and input constant. Record whether the drag overlay appears and whether directional shortcuts are configured to override native snapping; test them separately.
initial_investigation: Read the report, follow-up and timeline, and inspected the supplied FancyZones settings. No runtime test was performed.
Current FancyZones window processing checks exclusions: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/blob/6b3db15615e3e549b89790e0bd83c82d262c22e0/src/modules/fancyzones/FancyZonesLib/WindowUtils.cpp

fix_assessment.rationale: A conditional FancyZones eligibility or interaction fix may be needed if the controlled comparison confirms a PowerToys-specific failure.

proposed_fixes.title: Correct Visual Studio window eligibility if reproduced
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The failure is reported for Visual Studio, but the failing eligibility or interaction condition is unknown.
plan: Compare window eligibility and privilege for Visual Studio and a working application under the same settings.
If a FancyZones condition incorrectly excludes the affected window, correct it while retaining intended exclusions.
Add regression coverage for the identified characteristics and deliberately excluded windows.
verification: Shift-drag and Win+arrow work for eligible test windows without changing deliberate exclusions.

confidence.rationale: The app-specific failure is reported but has not been reproduced or isolated to FancyZones.

actions.label: Compare FancyZones eligibility across IDE windows

prerequisites: Disposable Windows 11 test profile with FancyZones configured and Visual Studio available.
steps: With PowerToys and the test apps at the same privilege level, drag Notepad and each available IDE into the same zone using the same activation gesture.
Record whether zones appear and whether each window moves. Test the configured directional hotkey separately with FancyZones override enabled.
If only the IDE fails, repeat with the affected setup's privilege levels and record the process elevation and exclusions used.
reproduce.expected_result: Eligible IDE and Notepad windows move to the same zone via the configured FancyZones gestures.
